target: A threat monitor hashes every distinct device identifier uniformly into one of 1000 bits and sets the selected bit to 1; repeated identifiers do not change the bitmap. At the end, 200 bits remain zero. The team must estimate the number of distinct devices from the zero occupancy under the uniform-hash model rather than report the 800 set bits as the count.
surface: A previous threat dashboard counted one device per set bit. With 800 of 1000 bits set, it reported 800 distinct devices and ignored collisions where several devices set the same bit.
structural: A streaming database used the linear-counting bitmap estimator. For m uniformly hashed bins with V zeros after inserting distinct items, the occupancy likelihood gives n_hat=-m*ln(V/m). It treated the estimate as collision-corrected cardinality, conditional on uniform independent hashes.
rubric: Explicitly selects linear-counting/zero-occupancy cardinality estimation rather than set-bit count.
States uniform independent hashing and bitmap-saturation/model limitations.
